data_analysis_biosamples_psychopathology

Nico Bast

2025-10-06

1 data analysis - SEGA biosamples psychopathology

Aim: relate biosample data (hair and saliva) to general psychopathology as preliminary work for LOCUS-MENTAL

1.1 read data

  • utilizes a master file of the SEGA data
#project location
root_path<-'C:/Users/nico/Nextcloud/project_sega'

#read after row 2
df<-read.xlsx(paste0(root_path,'/data/master_file_SEGA_data.xlsx'),na.strings = c("NA","-"),detectDates = T)

#take experimental data from ti
df_exp<-read.xlsx(paste0(root_path,'/data/master_file_SEGA_data_Sept2025.xlsx'),startRow = 3)
df_exp<-df_exp[,c(1,3,57:88)]

1.2 rename varibles

#saliva samples renaming
names(df)[31:40]<-paste0('saliva_',names(df)[31:40])

#hair renaming
names(df)[26]<-'hair_mass_mg'
names(df)[27]<-'hair_comments'
names(df)[28]<-'hair_cortisol_pg_mg'
names(df)[29]<-'hair_cortisone_pg_mg'

#SDQ
names(df)[41:46]<-c('SDQ_emo','SDQ_beh','SDQ_hyp','SDQ_beh_peers','SDQ_pros','SDQ_total')
names(df)[47:52]<-c('SDQ_emo','SDQ_beh','SDQ_hyp','SDQ_beh_peers','SDQ_pros','SDQ_total')


names(df)[41:46]<-paste0(names(df)[41:46],'_parent')
names(df)[47:52]<-paste0(names(df)[47:52],'_self')

#remove special characters
names(df)<-gsub('\\[','',names(df))
names(df)<-gsub('\\]','',names(df))
names(df)<-gsub('\\%','',names(df))

1.3 merge data

df<-merge(df,df_exp,by.x='SEGA_ID',by.y='ID_Studie')

1.4 data manipulation

1.4.1 remove outlier

hist(df$YSR_GES)

hist(df$YSR_T_GES)

df$YSR_T_GES[which(df$YSR_T_GES>100)]<-NA
df$YSR_T_GES[which(df$YSR_T_GES<25)]<-NA

1.4.2 create saliva change variable

df$saliva_change<-df$saliva_Average.2-df$saliva_Average.1

1.4.3 recode group variable

table(df$group)
## < table of extent 0 >
df$group<-ifelse(df$Gruppe %in% c('AUT','ASD'),'ASD',df$Gruppe)
df$autism_boolean<-ifelse(df$group=='ASD',T,F)

1.4.4 logarithmize bio samples

df$saliva_Average.1_log<-log10(df$saliva_Average.1)
df$saliva_Average.2_log<-log10(df$saliva_Average.2)
df$hair_cortisol_pg_mg_log<-log10(df$hair_cortisol_pg_mg)

df$saliva_change_log<-df$saliva_Average.2_log-df$saliva_Average.1_log

1.4.5 IQ estimate

df$iq<-with(df,(iq_mt+iq_gf+iq_mz+iq_wt)/4)

1.4.6 calculate age

df$Date<-as.Date(df$Date, format = "%m/%d/%y")
df$age<-as.numeric((df$Date-df$birth_date)/360)

hist(df$age)

1.4.7 estimate BMI

df$BMI<-with(df,Gewicht.kg/(Groeße.cm/100*Groeße.cm/100))

1.4.8 pupil measure averages

df$BPS_average<-(df$pd_low_oddball_saliencehigh_utilityhigh+
  df$pd_low_oddball_saliencehigh_utilitylow+
  df$pd_low_oddball_saliencelow_utilityhigh+
  df$pd_low_oddball_saliencelow_utilitylow+
  df$BPS_Oddball_before_forward+
  df$BPS_Oddball_after_forward+
  df$BPS_Oddball_before_reverse+
  df$BPS_Oddball_after_reverse)/8


df$SEPR_average<-(df$rpd_oddball_saliencehigh_utilityhigh+
                    df$rpd_oddball_saliencehigh_utilitylow+
                    df$rpd_oddball_saliencelow_utilityhigh+
                    df$rpd_oddball_saliencelow_utilitylow+
                    df$SEPR_Oddball_after_forward+
                    df$SEPR_Oddball_after_reverse+
                    df$SEPR_Oddball_before_forward+
                    df$SEPR_Oddball_before_reverse)/8

hist(df$BPS_average,20)

hist(df$SEPR_average,20)

1.4.9 pupil size changes

df$SEPR_Oddball_change<-df$SEPR_Oddball_after_forward-df$SEPR_Oddball_before_forward
df$BPS_change<-df$BPS_Standard_after_forward-df$BPS_Standard_before_forward

1.4.10 SDQ externalizing internalizing

df$SDQ_self_int<-df$SDQ_emo_self+df$SDQ_beh_peers_self
df$SDQ_self_ext<-df$SDQ_beh_self+df$SDQ_hyp_self

df$SDQ_parent_int<-df$SDQ_emo_parent+df$SDQ_beh_peers_parent
df$SDQ_parent_ext<-df$SDQ_beh_parent+df$SDQ_hyp_parent

1.4.11 global externalizing internalizing

df$INT_self<-rowMeans(scale(df$SDQ_self_int)+scale(df$YSR_T_INT))
df$EXT_self<-rowMeans(scale(df$SDQ_self_ext)+scale(df$YSR_T_EXT))

df$INT_parent<-rowMeans(scale(df$SDQ_parent_int)+scale(df$CBCL_T_INT))
df$EXT_parent<-rowMeans(scale(df$SDQ_parent_ext)+scale(df$CBCL_T_EXT))

hist(df$INT_self,20)

hist(df$EXT_self,20)

hist(df$INT_parent,20)

hist(df$EXT_parent,20)

1.5 data quality

1.5.1 missing data

-complete data for CBCL -more missings in SDQ

CBCL<-with(df,table(!is.na(CBCL_T_GES)))
YSR<-with(df,table(!is.na(YSR_T_GES)))

SDQ_self<-with(df,table(!is.na(SDQ_total_self)))
SDQ_parent<-with(df,table(!is.na(SDQ_total_parent)))

hair_cortisol<-with(df,table(!is.na(hair_cortisol_pg_mg)))
saliva_cortisol_measure1<-with(df,table(!is.na(saliva_Average.1)))
saliva_cortisol_measure2<-with(df,table(!is.na(saliva_Average.2)))

missing_table<-rbind(CBCL,YSR,SDQ_self,SDQ_parent,hair_cortisol,saliva_cortisol_measure1,saliva_cortisol_measure2)

1.5.6 covariates biosamples - influence of bio sample characteristics

  • considering: time of day, saliva measurement error, BMI, age, gender
  • higher saliva measurement error associated with lower saliva cortisol 1
  • higher age associated with higher saliva cortisol 1
  • higher hair mass associated with lower hair cortisol measure

–> time of day, gender, BMI is not associated with biosamples

lm<-lm(saliva_Average.1_log~saliva_Time.1+saliva_CV.1+BMI+age+gender,df)
anova(lm)
## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Response: saliva_Average.1_log
##               Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value   Pr(>F)   
## saliva_Time.1  1 0.1013 0.10127  2.2980 0.133005   
## saliva_CV.1    1 0.3529 0.35285  8.0066 0.005734 **
## BMI            1 0.0347 0.03473  0.7881 0.377019   
## age            1 0.3479 0.34786  7.8933 0.006074 **
## gender         1 0.0031 0.00305  0.0692 0.793034   
## Residuals     91 4.0104 0.04407                    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
standardize_parameters(lm)

1.6 data analysis

1.6.1 collapse CBCL and SDQ measures

  • does not suggest collapsing SDQ and CBCL/YSR reports of internalizing and externalizing
interested_variables<-c(
  "YSR_T_GES",
  "YSR_INT",
  "YSR_EXT",
  "CBCL_T_GES",
  "CBCL_T_INT",
  "CBCL_T_EXT",
  "SDQ_total_self",
  "SDQ_self_int",
  "SDQ_self_ext",
  "SDQ_total_parent",
  "SDQ_parent_int",
  "SDQ_parent_ext"
  
)

cor_matrix<-round(cor(df[,interested_variables],use = 'pairwise.complete.obs'),2)
corrplot(cor_matrix,type='upper',order='hclust',tl.cex=0.6)

df_cluster<-t(df[complete.cases(df[,interested_variables]),interested_variables])
df_cluster<-scale(df_cluster)
dist_matrix<-dist(df_cluster, method='euclidean')
dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist_matrix)


melted_dist <- reshape2::melt(dist_mat)
ggplot(melted_dist, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "red", high = "white") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Euclidean Distance Matrix", x = "", y = "")

1.6.2 correlation table

  • saliva cortisol is negatively associated with baseline pupil sizes

  • hair cortisol is negatively assoicated with self- and parent-reported internalizing

  • SEPR average is negatively associated with self- and parent-reported externalizing

  • BPS average is negatively associated with saliva cortisol

interested_variables<-c(
  "saliva_Average.1",
  "saliva_Average.2",
  'saliva_change',
  "hair_cortisol_pg_mg", 
  "BPS_change",
  'BPS_average',
  "SEPR_average",
  "SEPR_Oddball_change",
  "INT_parent",
  "EXT_parent",
  "CBCL_T_GES",
  "INT_self",
  "EXT_self",
  "YSR_T_GES"
)

cor_matrix<-round(cor(df[,interested_variables],use = 'pairwise.complete.obs'),2)
corrplot(cor_matrix,type='upper',order='hclust',tl.cex=0.6)

1.6.3 visualization

  • higher psychopathology seems to be associated with attenuated saliva cortisol drop-off during the experiment

1.6.4 effect of psychopathology on cortisol

  • higher self-reported psychopathology is associated with attenuated hair cortisol (hypocortisolism)
  • even when controlling for autism symptoms in the autism-enriched sample
  • can be attributed to internalizing versus externalizing symptoms
  • also after controlling for relevant covariates
#customaized ANOVA output
analyze_lm<-function(x,log_backtransform=F){
  print(car::Anova(x,type=3))
  return(cbind(round(summary(x)$coefficients[,1],2),round(confint(x),2)))
  
  if(log_backtransform){
  return(cbind(round(10^summary(x)$coefficients[,1],2),round(10^confint(x),2)))
  }
  
}

#scale numeric variables
df_scaled<-as.data.frame(lapply(df, function(x) {if (is.numeric(x)) scale(x) else x}))

1.6.7 cortisol and pupillary measures explaining self-reported internalizing

  • lower hair cortisol associated with higher internalizing psychopathology

  • higher BPS is associated with higher internalizing

  • the interaction suggests that this might be specifically relevant in groups of elevated symptoms

  • pupillary measures might be a quantitative predictor of internalizing psychopathology in at-risk children

1.6.8 cortisol and pupillary measures explaining self-reported externalizing

  • specific to SDQ externalizing

  • higher hair cortisol also associated with attenuated self-reported externalizing

  • however –> mediated by pupillary responses interaction

  • at above average BPS levels - lower SEPR predict elevated externalizing

  • in parent reports - lower SEPR is associated with increased externalizing

1.6.9 classification

  • above change classification based on pupillometry and cortisol measures
# Load necessary libraries
require(caret)
## Loading required package: caret
## Loading required package: lattice
require(pROC)
## Loading required package: pROC
## Type 'citation("pROC")' for a citation.
## 
## Attaching package: 'pROC'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     cov, smooth, var
require(boot)
## Loading required package: boot
## 
## Attaching package: 'boot'
## The following object is masked from 'package:lattice':
## 
##     melanoma
## The following object is masked from 'package:car':
## 
##     logit
df$YSR_INT_CUTOFF<-ifelse(df$YSR_T_INT>=65,T,F)
# Ensure the target variable is a factor
df$YSR_INT_CUTOFF <- as.factor(df$YSR_INT_CUTOFF)

table(df$YSR_INT_CUTOFF)
## 
## FALSE  TRUE 
##    96    57
#complete data
df_complete<-df[complete.cases(df$BPS_average) & 
                  complete.cases(df$SEPR_average) & 
                  complete.cases(df$hair_cortisol_pg_mg) & 
                  complete.cases(df$saliva_Average.1) & complete.cases(df$YSR_INT_CUTOFF),]


# Split data into training and testing sets
set.seed(838)
trainIndex <- createDataPartition(df_complete$YSR_INT_CUTOFF, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
trainData <- df[trainIndex, ]
testData <- df[-trainIndex, ]

# Fit logistic regression model
model0 <- glm(YSR_INT_CUTOFF ~ hair_cortisol_pg_mg + saliva_Average.1, 
             data = trainData, family = binomial)

model1 <- glm(YSR_INT_CUTOFF ~ BPS_average*SEPR_average, 
             data = trainData, family = binomial)

model2 <- glm(YSR_INT_CUTOFF ~ BPS_average*SEPR_average + hair_cortisol_pg_mg + saliva_Average.1, 
             data = trainData, family = binomial)


# Predict probabilities on test set
probabilities0 <- predict(model0, newdata = testData, type = "response")
probabilities1 <- predict(model1, newdata = testData, type = "response")
probabilities2 <- predict(model2, newdata = testData, type = "response")
#probabilities <- predict(model, type = "response")

# Compute AUC
roc_obj0 <- roc(testData$YSR_INT_CUTOFF, probabilities0)
## Setting levels: control = FALSE, case = TRUE
## Setting direction: controls < cases
roc_obj1 <- roc(testData$YSR_INT_CUTOFF, probabilities1)
## Setting levels: control = FALSE, case = TRUE
## Setting direction: controls > cases
roc_obj2 <- roc(testData$YSR_INT_CUTOFF, probabilities2)
## Setting levels: control = FALSE, case = TRUE
## Setting direction: controls < cases
#roc_obj <- roc(df_complete$YSR_INT_CUTOFF, probabilities)

auc_value0 <- auc(roc_obj0)
auc_value1 <- auc(roc_obj1)
auc_value2 <- auc(roc_obj2)

# Print AUC
print(paste("AUC:", round(auc_value2,3)))
## [1] "AUC: 0.655"
plot(roc_obj0, main = "ROC Curve")
lines(roc_obj1, col='red')
lines(roc_obj2, col='blue')
legend("right", legend = c("Cortisol", "Pupillometry","Cortisol+Pupillometry"),
       col = c("black","red","blue"), lwd = 2)

# Bootstrapping function to compute AUC
boot_auc <- function(data, indices) {
  d <- data[indices, ]
  model <- glm(YSR_INT_CUTOFF ~ BPS_average*SEPR_average + hair_cortisol_pg_mg + saliva_Average.1, data = d, family = binomial)
  probs <- predict(model, newdata = testData, type = "response")
  roc_obj <- roc(testData$YSR_INT_CUTOFF, probs)
  return(auc(roc_obj))
}

# Combine training data and testData for bootstrapping
# (You can also bootstrap on testData if preferred)
set.seed(123)
boot_results <- boot(data = df_complete, statistic = boot_auc, R = 1000)
